title: Party Animal
text: “Guh! I can’t afford to go down here! Not this time, not again, no way in hell!”
Itsuki, who should’ve been paralyzed, popped back up after chugging some medicine and got right back in the fight. Persistent, I say-pyon!
“Naofumi-san!”
“That trick won’t work twice, I say-pyoon!”
Tsk tsk tsk! I taunted him.
“Vof! Spiral Claw X!”
“Whoops! Go ahead and spin that big wheel of yours right into Ren, I say-pyon!”
I deflected Wolf’s charge and sent it careening straight into Ren.
“Get out of my way!”
“Vofuuuu!?”
Ren batted Wolf aside too, and the poor thing went tumbling gracelessly across the ground.
“Hmm… not bad footwork.”
“Hmm… is that the Spear Hero’s serious mode?”
“No, I can see it clearly… he still has plenty left in the tank.”
Granny and Panda’s grandfather had wandered over to watch our battle too, it seemed. This was starting to feel like a proper spectacle, I say.
“Wolf’s outclassed. Say what you will, but they really are Four Cardinal Heroes.”
“They look like adorable demi-humans now, but the power hidden underneath is terrifying.”
“It’s all cute on the outside but the fight’s happening on a whole different level—can Ren and Itsuki even get their revenge on Motoyasu-kun?”
“Might be tough-nano. Spear Hero, whatever spearmanship that person taught him really sank into his bones-nano. His precision’s sharp-nano.”

Fuhahaha! It’s not just my weapon that’s been powered up—my technique itself has leveled up far beyond before, I say! Even I found it a bit uncanny how smoothly I was parrying Itsuki and Ren’s furious onslaught!
“Whoa, what’s going on? Looks fun!”
“Motoyasu-sama! Fight on!”
“Ooh, go get ’em, pet dog!”
“Ohh…”

Yuki-chan and the other Filolial-sama seemed to have joined in cheering, too. Things were getting rather lively. And so, after the fierce battle raged on, in the end I was the only one left standing, I say-pyon!
“I did it, Father! I’m the champion, I say-pyon! And the champion’s prize is the right to be petted by Father, I say-pyoon!”

Ren and Itsuki lay sprawled unconscious, thoroughly incapacitated. They’d put up quite a fight, but my victory was never in doubt. Wolf, naturally, had already gone down as well. I struck a victory pose and hoisted my spear high.
“The matter of the champion’s prize seems to have been decided without anyone’s input.”
“Next up, Rabbit Guy! Get in the ring too, I say-pyon! Now that everyone knows I’m an usaunny, that position belongs to me, I say-pyon!”
“Just what on earth is this man even competing over?! Actually, what even is he?!”
“Ah… well, anyway, Motoyasu-kun. It’s time for a little lecture, don’t you think?”
And so, somehow, I ended up on the receiving end of Father’s scolding. Utterly unreasonable, I say. Winning a tournament and getting no reward whatsoever—what is the meaning of this!

“Father, do you look upon these unclouded eyes of mine and still believe I’ve done wrong? I merely taught Ren and Itsuki the truth of this world, and bestowed upon them the magic of becoming heroes beloved by all, I say-pyon.”
“Ugh… all I can say is that he’s giving me those eyes—visible from a mile away even in usaunny form—of someone who believes with their whole heart that they’ve done nothing wrong.”
“Ugh, those sparkly eyes are gross-nano. And he knows full well Naofumi’s weak to that look-nano, so he’s going all out with it-nano.”
“Rival, don’t say such hurtful things, I say-pyon.”
I haven’t done anything wrong, I say-pyon.
“The ones at fault are Itsuki, who got carried away, and his so-called companions, who sold him off without even noticing his form had changed, I say-pyon.”
Ren, at least, was clearly still coordinating properly with his companions, and he was wide awake now too.
“I can’t really argue with that part, but I do wish you’d let things play out a little more before stepping in.”
“I figured it’d be fine, I say-pyon. It’s just that those guys were too foolish, I say-pyon.”
“Hmm… well, since Ren’s companions actually held it together, I guess I can’t fully dismiss Motoyasu-kun’s logic either.”
My conduct was entirely justified, I say-pyon.
“Can’t really say that-nano. In another loop, the Bow Hero got killed by his own companions-nano.”
“Rival, don’t you dare try to pin that on me, I say-pyon!”
Sure, in the loop where we went to Siltvelt, Itsuki did end up killed by his companions, but the circumstances back then were completely different from this time.
“I made sure things never got to the point where he’d be forced to watch himself lose face-to-face and his companions would try to jump ship, I say.”
That should settle the matter of Itsuki’s innocence—well, my innocence—on that front.
“As for Ren looking pathetic, that’s Rafumi’s fault, not mine, I say-pyon… I wish people would stop pinning everything on me, I say.”
“And now he’s deflecting blame too. The root cause here is that you turned him into an inult, Motoyasu-kun.”

“In other loops, Ren didn’t change much even after becoming an inult, I say-pyon. Once you’re riding the winning horse, you get cocky regardless, so really it was just an experiment to see what would happen if I made him one, I say-pyon.”
Since it seemed like it’d take Kuro-chan a while to awaken as the Dark Saint Hero, I gave him a bit of trouble to stall him, and as a result, he ended up coming to Father’s side, I say-pyon.
“If you’d sent him back sooner… well, I might’ve believed you.”
“Was that really necessary, I say-pyon? In the end, Ren figured out the truth about Melromarc and the conspiracy anyway, I say-pyon.”
“Hmm… I think the problem is the malice behind it.”
“There’s no malice in me whatsoever, I say-pyon. Ren was purely incidental, I say-pyon.”

“That’s somehow a worse answer than malice… it basically means you don’t care either way. I always figured you had that streak in you, Motoyasu-kun, but I don’t think that’s something you should just admit so plainly.”
Regardless of the details, Father declared that Motoyasu-kun needed to reflect on what he’d done.
“Unreasonable, I say. I won the tournament and there’s no reward whatsoever, I sayyyy!”
“After pulling off all that and striking a victory pose amid a literal pile of bodies… I mean, should I really pet him?”
“Ngh… gah… we’re not… beaten yet.”
“Remember this, I say.”
Ren and Itsuki, now awake, groaned out their frustration.
“Can’t be helped, I say. Very well, I shall return Ren and Itsuki to their original forms, I say.”
“Hurry up and change me back!”
Ren looked desperate to return as soon as possible, but Itsuki seemed rather indifferent about the whole thing.
“Not particularly interested, personally. What’s the best way to get back at Motoyasu-san, I wonder.”
“Itsuki! You can go back to normal! Why aren’t you jumping at the chance right now?!”
“Well, sure, but… being asked if I want to go back to being a so-called superior being, a human, at this point kind of feels beside the point…”
“Hmph! Never mind Itsuki—just hurry up and turn me back into a human already!”
Ren was quite desperate about it, I must say.
“Ren, perhaps you ought to relax a little, hm? Allow this usaunny to show off a bit of his charm, I say.”
“Motoyasu-kun somehow seems to have pride even about being an usaunny.”
“Fuhahaha, this fur of mine exists solely to be petted by Father. So, Father! How about it—pet this fur of mine, I say-pyon!”
I nuzzled up against Father, practically begging to be petted. My eyes were positively sparkling, I say.
“Naofumi, if you don’t pet this Spear Hero, he’s going to keep nuzzling up with those eyes forever-nano.”
Rival let out a sigh. Say whatever you like, I say.
“Once you feel the texture of my fur, Father, you’ll surely realize there’s no value whatsoever in touching something like Rabbit Guy, I say.”
“Just what exactly is this man competing over?!”
“Sigh… honestly, no helping it, is there.”
Father sighed and reached out to stroke my fur.
“Whoa, what is this texture— it’s so silky-smooth, like a stuffed animal, I can barely tell it’s a living creature.”
“Fluffy, isn’t it, Father? How is it, hm?”
“I mean, yeah, I can tell you’re really particular about your coat.”
“Vof, Naofumi-sama, me too! Pet me too, vof!”
“Wolf, are you trying to compete with me too, I say?!”
“Vof-pen!”

Curse you, Wolf! Not content with trying to gain the upper hand over Rabbit Guy through fur in wolf form, are you now trying to compete even in peckul form?! Just how cunning can one creature be, I say!
